author: Michal238
text:
It's all about FTR's. Most recent peak doesn't tell you what is going
on you need to mark FTR's within it, and check what it is reacting to.

On nasdaq there was nice FTR ( 24 Jul), but as we know price can make FO
 above FTR and then reverse. Go to your charts and check M1 above FTR in
 order to see where price bounced from. There is very nice minor FTR,
great place for FO.

How could we know if price is going to bounce there? Well, there was no
engulf before price reached this level, but compression on approach told
 us what IT's intentions are. So it was very low risk trade with TG1 on
 next FTR below.

Hi xman,

It's time I schould write little summary of what I've been doing recently.

I traded small live account for few weeks. Unfortunately I realized that
 although I have enough knowledge to make good returns on forex, I'm not
 able to make use of it yet. It was first time I traded with real money
 and I was doing crazy things. It was just chaos - I missed most of
great entries while taking unconfirmed and experimental trades.

I did't have trade plan - I just wanted to watch many pairs and take
trade when I see opportunity. This just couldn't work with my character
and lack of experiance. In second week I took over 20 trades - most of
them were unconfirmed touch trades. So after few weeks I decided to take
 a break from charts for few days. When I look at account history and I
put on charts my trades I can't believe what I was doing. Once I tried
to catch one move three times and I was stopped out because I did't
analyse it properly and my read was just wrong.

I put this post on my desktop:

Such a wise words.

Now, I gained some experiance and I know what trading with real money is
 like. So I read again IFs and master traders posts - now I can look at

concept separately to organize my knowledge better and I'll tie it
together with PAZ.

author: Michal238
text:
I decided to share with you guys this analysis and my trade and stupid
 exit which was probably the most unreasonable thing i did since I
started live trading.

I have a bit more than 1:10 RR on that but it feels like consolation
prize. I hope that you will learn something from my mistakes.

And now important question: why the hell did I exit there? It was an impulse - I couldn't look at this situation objectively.

I entered with too big position size. I finally had opportunity to get a
 trade with massive RR and really big profits. I did't want to mess it
up ( which I did )

When I was in profit ( 1:10 RR) I was checking if I analysed evrything correctly. And I found this...

I thought: what it price wants to visit this QM lvl?

Taking profits was very tempting so I colsed it before retrace, hoping
that I'll enter again on this QM lvl or lower if PA shows signs of
reversal...

While I was focusing on details to much I ignored basic concepts - this
was complete QM setup. If price were to visit this QM lvl I found, then
there would be a diamond not QM. Right schoulder would reach extreme
orders breaking above FO.

It was very important lesson for me and I hope that things I learned
about setups like this and about myself will help to prevent situation
like this in the future.

Pieces of RTM puzzle are getting together. I must now do something about
 my reckless trading and bad money managment. If my other trades will go
 well

I'll finish this week with decent profit, but I know that I'm able to make so much more with things I learned on RTM.
